# Parameter automation

Automation changes an instrument or mixer parameter over Score time.
Automatable BlueSynthBuilder controls, mixer levels, sends, and effects
can provide targets. The automation line is stored with the project,
while CSD generation supplies the Csound control signal. See
[BlueSynthBuilder](instruments.qmd) for instrument controls and
[Mixer](mixer.qmd) for channel routing.

## Assign a target

On a PolyObject's SoundObject layer or a Track layer, open its **Automation
(A)** button and choose an available parameter. Choosing a target assigned to
another layer moves the assignment; choosing one assigned here removes it. Use
**Clear All** to remove this layer's assignments. **Cleanup Missing** removes
references to parameters no longer present in the project. Keep each parameter
assigned to one intended layer to avoid competing automation lines.

## Edit lines

The Score toolbar has **Score**, **Single Line**, and **Multi Line** modes.
Use Score mode for SoundObjects. In Single Line mode, select a layer's
parameter and edit its points on the line. Multi Line mode lets you select
and move points across visible lines. Hover over or select a point to read its
numeric beat and value on the canvas. Blue edits points graphically; it does
not offer a numeric time/value editor. Check the layer and selected parameter
before dragging: automation edits change the project and the generated CSD.

Preview a short range with **Project → Generate CSD to Screen** or render
it to check the result. When coding a BlueSynthBuilder instrument or
effect, place an automatable replacement key where a Csound control-rate
value is legal; an unautomated parameter may be emitted as a constant.

The older manual's exact colors, point gestures, and keyboard shortcuts
were tied to the Java timeline. Follow the controls shown by the current
Score editor for those gestures.
